in-vīsĭbĭlis , e, adj.,
I.invisible, unseen (post-Aug.): “foramina, Cels. praef.: terra,” Tert. adv. Herm. 29 init. : “deus,” Lact. 7, 9 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 35, 208; Tert. Carn. Chr. 12: “ea in nobis sunt meliora, quae sunt invisibilia,” Aug. Ep. 159, 3 : “opera ad illos dies invisibiles pertinentia, quibus creavit omnia,” i. e. when there was no human eye to see, Aug. de Gen. 6, 6 init. al.—Adv.: in-vīsĭbĭlĭter , invisibly, Tert. adv. Val. 14; Aug. de Gen. 6, 6, 10.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
